title: Submit a Time Off Request
goal: Request one day of vacation, get it released by Payroll, and confirm approval.
context: Sample lesson that exercises every step type. People often stop at Save Draft and assume Payroll can see it, or submit and never tell Payroll, so the request sits unreleased.

steps.title: Start a request
steps.instruction: Start a new time off request.
steps.why: Every absence starts as its own request, so Payroll can release it and your manager can plan around it.
hints: Look near the top right of the Time Off page.
The button is labeled New Request. If you are on the History page, go back to Time Off first.

commonMistakes.say: History only shows past requests. To start one, go back to Time Off and choose New Request.

steps.title: Choose the absence type
steps.why: The type decides which balance the hours come out of.
hints: Absence Type is the first dropdown on the form.
Open the dropdown and choose Vacation, not Sick or Personal Day.

steps.title: Choose the reason code
steps.why: Reason codes feed the reports your department reviews each month.
hints: Reason Code is right below Absence Type.

steps.title: Enter the dates
steps.instruction: Enter a Start Date and an End Date for your day off.
hints: For one day off, Start Date and End Date are the same day.
Fill in both date fields. The step completes when both have a date.

steps.title: Check your balance
steps.instruction: Before you submit, confirm you have enough vacation hours. Your balance is on the right side panel.
steps.why: A request that exceeds your balance gets sent back, and you lose a day waiting.

steps.title: Submit the request
hints: The Submit button is at the bottom of the form.

commonMistakes.say: Save Draft keeps it private. Payroll never sees a draft. Use Submit.

steps.title: Hand it to Payroll
steps.instruction: Let Payroll know you submitted it. They release it on their side.
steps.why: The system does not notify Payroll. Until someone tells them, the request just sits.

steps.title: Confirm coverage
steps.instruction: Call your manager to confirm coverage for your day off.

prep.goal: Confirm who covers your work and get a verbal yes.
prep.opener: Hi, quick one. I put in for Friday off and want to make sure coverage is set.

pushbacks.try: Offer a specific handoff: who covers what, and that you will brief them Thursday.

doThis: State the purpose in your first sentence.
End with a clear next step.

callouts.say: In Facilities, time off during the first week of the month needs director sign-off first.
Pick Other here, not Personal. Our reports read Other for this case.

reminders.say: Check that your time off request was approved. If not, contact Payroll.

recap.summary: You submitted a time off request, handed it to Payroll, and confirmed coverage.
nextSteps: Watch for the approval reminder in 3 days.
